This guide walks through installing the Widget command line client, authenticating it against your workspace, and verifying that the connection works.
Install the CLI
The client ships as a single binary with no runtime dependencies. Download the archive for your platform and put the binary somewhere on your PATH.
curl -fsSL https://widget.example.com/install.sh | sh
widget --version
If you prefer a package manager, the Homebrew tap and the Scoop bucket are both updated for every release.
Configure the client
Run the login command once per machine. It stores a scoped token in your user configuration directory and refreshes it automatically before it expires.
widget login --workspace acme
widget config set region eu-west
Configuration values can also come from environment variables, which take precedence over the file. This is useful in CI, where you should use a short-lived token.
Tokens created for CI should be limited to the repositories the job actually needs.
Once the client is configured, run the doctor command to confirm that the binary, the token, and the network path all agree.
